### 1.  Express \(10^{100}S\)

For each \(n\)

\[
\frac{10^{100}}{10^{\,n}-1}

Thus every term of \(10^{100}S\) is a power of ten.  
Collect terms having the same power.

Let  

\[
d=n(k+1)\qquad (1\le d\le 100).
\]

Then the exponent of the power of ten is

\[
e=100-d,\qquad 0\le e\le 99.
\]

The number of ordered pairs \((n,k)\) giving the same \(d\) is precisely the
number of positive divisors of \(d\), denoted \(\tau(d)\).
Hence

\[
10^{100}S=\sum_{e=0}^{99}\tau(100-e)\;10^{\,e}
          =\sum_{d=1}^{100}\tau(d)\;10^{\,100-d}.   \tag{1}
\]

\text{units}   &= \tau(100)=9,\\[2pt]
\text{tens}    &= \tau(99)=6,\\[2pt]
\text{hundreds}&= \tau(98)=6.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
\lfloor10^{100}S\rfloor \equiv 6\cdot10^2+6\cdot10+9
                          =669 \pmod{1000}.
\]
